questions.q: Why is a file-arrival trigger especially useful for this course's own Auto Loader ingestion work?
options: It is the default trigger type for every job
It is the only trigger type that supports retries
It requires no compute cluster at all
It starts a job run the moment new data actually lands, instead of guessing at a fixed schedule
questions.explain: File arrival triggers avoid the timing guesswork of a fixed schedule by starting the moment new files actually appear.

questions.q: What does a job-level retry policy control?
options: The order tasks run in
How many times a failed task retries, and how long to wait between attempts
Whether a job can be triggered manually
Which cluster type a task uses
questions.explain: Retry policy is a job-level setting for automatic retry behavior on failure, applying to every task in the job.

questions.q: What does a job-level timeout control?
options: How many tasks a job can contain
How long a run is allowed to take before it's automatically killed
How often the job's schedule triggers
Which workspace the job runs in
questions.explain: A timeout caps the maximum duration of a run, protecting against a runaway job without custom code.
